principle: Portable meaning is authoritative; each target maps roles, state and evidence without importing another toolkit's component model.

rows.portable: A role says what a thing is for, and is bound to a token on each substrate: surface, ink, hairline, accent, focus, and the three conditions. A component names the role and is written once.
rows.web: Generated CSS custom properties, rebound by the substrate attribute.
rows.android: Generated Kotlin colour maps, one per substrate.
rows.native: Generated Rust structs, one per substrate, bound to the contract's own constants.
rows.gate: Every role binds to a token the contract has, and every role pairing that carries text measures 4.5 on both substrates.

rows.portable: The components the field agrees on, stated as roles, states, geometry, typography and the accessibility they owe. The names come from a measurement of the field, not from a preference.
rows.web: Generated stylesheet, rendered by a renderer that is generic: a component is added by stating it, not by adding a case to the renderer.
rows.android: Not yet projected. The roles are; the components are not.
rows.native: Not yet projected. The roles are; the components are not.
rows.gate: The stylesheet is what the specification projects, every token a component names is one the contract has, and every variant reads on its own background.

rows.portable: Space Grotesk is the visual/interface family, including metadata and technical strings.
rows.web: Packaged variable WOFF2 via @font-face; inherited by body, controls, code and metadata.
rows.android: Packaged variable TTF in res/font and explicit Compose FontFamily.
rows.native: Packaged variable TTF registered with the GPUI text system; family selected as Space Grotesk.
rows.gate: Rendered family resolves to Space Grotesk and required French/symbol glyphs are present.

rows.portable: Exact values originate in core/TOKENS.json; contrast rules are semantic constraints, not theme suggestions.
rows.native: Rust constants or theme values generated from the same token source; no handwritten second palette.

rows.portable: Principal contextual operation with verb label, focus treatment and explicit pending/result distinction.
rows.android: Compose Button with semantic label/state and minimum target area.
rows.native: Focusable GPUI action element with keyboard activation, visible focus and explicit accessible state.
rows.gate: Keyboard/touch activation and focus are observable without hue alone.

rows.portable: Intended, observed and projected values remain separate; mutation intent never becomes success evidence by itself.
rows.web: projectState(requested, observed) returns pending until authoritative observation matches.
rows.android: StateProjection.kt retains requested and observed separately.
rows.native: View model stores intent and observation separately; rendered status derives from both.
rows.gate: A request produces pending text before any success text.

rows.portable: State is text first, optionally reinforced by a small pip; status capsules are prohibited.
rows.web: Text status row plus optional ::before pip.
rows.android: Text with semantics stateDescription; optional adjacent dot, never a decorative chip.
rows.native: Text status and optional painted state pip; selection remains structural.
rows.gate: Meaning remains when color is removed.

rows.portable: Geometry, material, chrome, depth, content, hit region and allocation are independently representable.
rows.web: DOM/layout geometry; background/paint; border/focus chrome; shadow/recess depth; semantic content and hit target.
rows.android: Layout/Shape; Brush/Painter; border/focus semantics; shadow/draw layer; composable content and pointer target.
rows.native: GPUI layout/element hull; background or custom paint; border/focus styling; shadow/custom draw; content and hit testing.
rows.gate: Changing material does not silently change semantic role or hit geometry.

rows.portable: A field declares quantity, range, endpoints, neutral point when applicable, missing state and legend.
rows.web: CSS/SVG/canvas rendering paired with textual legend and missing-state handling.
rows.android: Brush/canvas rendering paired with semantics and textual legend.
rows.native: Shader/custom paint may render the field, but semantic metadata remains outside the shader and inspectable.
rows.gate: Unknown is not encoded as zero and the field is interpretable without decorative color assumptions.

rows.portable: Motion explains causality, is interruptible and preserves meaning in reduced-motion mode. Declared in full by profiles/motion/motion.json.
rows.web: prefers-reduced-motion removes nonessential duration while state changes remain textual.
rows.android: Platform reduced-motion/animation policy is respected by the consuming app; state text remains authoritative.
rows.native: Application motion policy gates transitions; state changes cancel superseded motion and never depend on animation alone.
rows.gate: Reduced motion preserves order, state and action meaning.

rows.portable: An alpha identity master is a compositing variant whose opaque pixels are byte-identical to the ratified master. It is sanctioned on neutral substrates only; over a chromatic substrate the opaque master is used.
rows.web: Neutral-surface placement only; the substrate behind an alpha mark is declared, not incidental.
rows.android: Neutral-surface placement only; alpha compositing is a declared surface decision rather than a draw-order side effect.
rows.native: Neutral-surface placement only; the mark is composited onto a surface that has been chosen and can be named.
rows.gate: Over Signal Orange, Royal Blue or Beret Green the opaque master appears, and the cube's dark faces stay distinguishable from the surface.

rows.portable: The token source, exported in the formats other tools already read.
rows.web: The DTCG and Style Dictionary exports under profiles/interchange/.
rows.android: Not applicable: the exports are for tools that read tokens.
rows.native: Not applicable, for the same reason.
rows.gate: tools/export_tokens.py --check: the exports match the token source.
